CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is currently on prednisone 1 mg daily and reports this dose is adequate for symptom control. She occasionally takes an extra prednisone dose approximately once per week due to increased foot pain, particularly on days when she is more active. Patient works a desk job. Methotrexate has been beneficial for joint pain. Patient held methotrexate for one week around her first COVID vaccine due to concern it could reduce vaccine efficacy; she felt significantly worse during that week without it. She continued methotrexate with her second COVID vaccine dose after consulting a hotline. Patient reports easy bruising with minor trauma, which the physician attributes to prednisone. She notes bruises appear without her noticing the initial injury. She has pain in her hand and foot joints, though knee pain has improved since the methotrexate dose was increased. She denies specific knowledge of when bruises occur.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for joint pain in hands and feet, occasional bruising, and nail ridges from psoriasis. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily, Methotrexate (dose recently increased).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a desk job. Pain increases on days off with increased activity.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Toes: good range of motion. Nails: ridges present from psoriasis. Knee: pain improved with flexion since methotrexate dose increase. Hand and foot joints examined.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis on prednisone and methotrexate with good response. Discontinue prednisone today. Continue methotrexate. Schedule blood work at front desk. Monitor for improvement in bruising after prednisone discontinuation. Follow-up in 3 months.
